sights.w: Palace of the Ryūkyū Kingdom from 1429 to 1879 and the centrepiece of the UNESCO Gusuku Sites. Destroyed in 1945 and again by fire in 2019; the rebuilt Seiden (main hall) exterior is complete, its interior due to reopen on 23 November 2026.
sights.k: UNESCO World Heritage gusuku; Seiden rebuild

sights.w: Limestone tomb of the second Shō dynasty, built in 1501 under King Shō Shin and modelled on Shuri Castle, its balustrades carved with dragons, phoenixes and lions. A National Treasure as well as a UNESCO component.

sights.n: Sonohyan-utaki Ishimon (園比屋武御嶽石門)
sights.address: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Stone gate to the sacred grove behind it, where Ryūkyū kings prayed for safe journeys before leaving Shuri; a UNESCO component standing beside Shuri Castle Park.

The Ryūkyū royal family’s largest villa garden, built around a pond with jagged coral-limestone bridges two kilometres south of Shuri Castle; used to receive Chinese envoys and now a UNESCO component.
Okinawa’s ichinomiya (chief shrine), perched on a coral bluff above Naminoue Beach; long the place where fishermen and sailors prayed for a safe voyage.

sights.n: Makishi Public Market (第一牧志公設市場)
sights.w: Naha’s kitchen since 1950: 75 ground-floor stalls of spiny lobster, reef fish, pork and island produce, with upstairs restaurants that cook what you buy (mochiage). Reopened in a new building on 19 March 2023.
The holiest site of Ryūkyūan religion: a sacred grove of limestone clefts overlooking Kudaka Island, where the kingdom’s high priestess was invested. A UNESCO Gusuku component.
Best-preserved of the Ryūkyū castle ruins: six enclosures of curved limestone walls on a ridge above both coasts. UNESCO Gusuku component.
Hilltop stronghold of the Hokuzan kingdom with long serpentine limestone walls. UNESCO Gusuku component.
Early-15th-century gusuku on a Yomitan hilltop, one of the five castle sites inscribed by UNESCO.
Terraced gusuku ruins on the Katsuren peninsula, one of the five castle sites inscribed by UNESCO.
